Exercise A

Proud to Be Black

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

Being proud to be Black means celebrating a rich and varied culture — its music, fashion, hairstyles, language and history — while also confronting how that culture is treated by the wider world. In recent years, the debate around cultural appropriation has become impossible to ignore. Cultural appropriation happens when members of a dominant culture adopt elements of a minority culture, often without understanding their significance or crediting where they came from.

Hairstyles are a striking example. For decades, Black women and men were told that braids, cornrows and afros looked "unprofessional", and many workplaces and schools enforced strict rules against them. Yet when the same hairstyles appear on non-Black celebrities, they are frequently praised as "edgy" or "new". Critics argue this double standard strips a style of its cultural meaning while denying Black people the very acceptance they were once refused.

Musicians, athletes and writers have increasingly spoken out, arguing that appreciation and appropriation are not the same thing. Appreciation, they say, involves learning about a culture's history, giving credit and supporting the community it comes from; appropriation simply borrows the surface without any of that respect.

For many young Black people today, pride is not just about looking back at history — it is about insisting that their culture be recognised, respected and fairly rewarded in the present.

Comprehension Questions

1 The text says that being proud to be Black also means how that culture is treated by the wider world.

2 Cultural appropriation happens when someone borrows cultural elements without understanding their significance or where they came from.

3 For decades, Black hairstyles such as braids and afros were often called in workplaces and schools.

4 When the same hairstyles appear on non-Black celebrities, one word often used to praise them is .

5 Critics say this double standard denies Black people the acceptance they were once .

6 According to the text, true appreciation involves learning a culture's history, giving credit and the community it comes from.
